data.title: Sub-agent
data.tagline: A separate agent the main agent assigns to a bounded part of a larger task
data.learningOutcome: You can identify work suited to a sub-agent and specify its scope, deliverable, and synthesis path.
data.description: Before release, a main agent can ask one sub-agent to review copy and another to check mobile layout, then combine their evidence. Each sub-agent needs a clear scope, permissions, and expected return.

learning.assumes: You have seen a complex task split into research, implementation, testing, or review.
learning.outcome: You can identify work suited to a sub-agent and specify its scope, deliverable, and synthesis path.

explanation.title: Split bounded work first
explanation.text: Assign separate accessibility, test, or documentation checks with clear read/write boundaries and completion criteria.

explanation.title: Work in separate context
explanation.text: Each sub-agent can focus on its own evidence and tools, returning only the relevant conclusions.

explanation.title: The main agent synthesizes
explanation.text: It waits for required evidence, resolves overlap or conflict, and forms one final result. Shared-file edits need clear ownership or sequencing.

data.boundary: Sub-agent behavior varies by product, including inherited context, permissions, and concurrency. A Skill is reusable task knowledge; a sub-agent is an agent performing delegated work.

lessonPractice.title: Before release, accessibility, API error handling, and test gaps must be reviewed. All three checks are read-only and can produce independent evidence. What is the better arrangement?

options.label: Assign one read-only subagent to each scoped check, then have the main agent wait, deduplicate, and summarize
options.feedback: Correct. Independent read-only checks parallelize well, while the main agent still resolves overlapping or conflicting findings.

options.label: Have three subagents rewrite the same configuration file at once without ownership boundaries
options.feedback: Concurrent writes to the same file can conflict or overwrite work. Define ownership or make changes serially after synthesis.

options.label: Give several subagents the same instruction to check everything, without scope, evidence requirements, or a return format
options.feedback: Unbounded delegation creates duplication, gaps, and results that are difficult to combine.

data.agentPrompt: Split this pre-release review across three read-only subagents: one for accessibility, one for API error handling, and one for test gaps. Each must return file locations and evidence without editing code. Wait for all three, merge duplicates, and produce one risk-ranked list. Ask me before making changes.
